headline: Analysts expect profits of America's biggest companies to jump about 31% in the third quarter, with AI-linked firms supplying most of the rise.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the Reuters report is from 9 Oct 2026 and reached the pool only through a 11 Oct rewrite, though the forecast is still current ahead of earnings season.
importance_line: What changed is that the expected profit growth of large US companies now leans on AI-linked firms, which matters first to savers and pension holders in US share funds, then to investors judging how long the rally can last, then to the companies named, and the doubt is that these are analysts' forecasts, which strategists say may be near their peak.
summary: Reuters reported on 9 Oct 2026, in a story Yahoo Finance republished in rewritten form on 11 Oct, that analysts expect profits of S&P 500 companies, the 500 large US listed firms behind the main share index, to rise about 31% in the third quarter from a year earlier, with the technology sector and AI heavyweights Alphabet, Amazon and Meta supplying about two-thirds of the rise, according to Tajinder Dhillon of the data firm LSEG. The growth is slower than the nearly 54% of the second quarter, and Anthony Saglimbene of Ameriprise Financial says investors fear growth is nearing its peak because the AI trade depends on continued heavy spending.
notes: Older news re-dated: Reuters original 9 Oct 2026 (read via KFGO's copy); the pool link is InvestorsHub's rewrite on Yahoo Finance, 11 Oct 2026. Not previously carried in our editions; the QA stale rule may hold it.
